_comment: Alfred provider registry — every model surface Alfred can dispatch work to.
Alfred's ORG ROLES (c-suite, vp, manager, employee, intern) are provider-neutral: they
describe a job, not a vendor. This file is the only place that says which model fills which
role for a given provider, so a user with Gemini + Ollama and no Claude still gets a working
org. Add a provider by adding a block here — no code change required.
cost: 'subscription' = flat rate already paid, zero marginal cost per call
'metered'      = billed per token, real money per call
'local'        = runs on the user's own hardware, free
roles: model id per org role. null means 'let the provider pick its default'.
approval: 'ask-per-use' means Alfred MUST get the operator's yes before each call.

claude.label: Claude (Anthropic)
claude.loginCmd: claude  (sign in on first run, or /login)
claude.notes: Usually the HOST that runs Alfred itself. Reached as the main loop and via the Agent tool, not through provider-run.

gemini.label: Gemini (Google, via Antigravity CLI)
gemini.loginCmd: agy  (first run opens a browser; use a Google AI Pro/Ultra account)

overflowModels._comment: Antigravity also serves these on the GOOGLE subscription — verified 2026-08-15. Reach with --model when Anthropic limits are the binding constraint, not by default.

routeFor: Anything enormous: sprawling docs, whole-codebase reads, long transcripts. 1M-token context.
Anything visual or recorded: it natively ingests images, audio and video (900 images, ~1h video, ~9.5h audio per call) rather than needing them described.
Fast first-pass analysis where latency matters — fastest of the three at ~138 t/s.
OVERFLOW CAPACITY: `agy models` also serves claude-opus-4-6-thinking and claude-sonnet-4-6 on the Google subscription. Verified working. Useful when Anthropic limits are the binding constraint.
neverRouteFor: Image GENERATION. Gemini's image models are excellent but the Antigravity CLI exposes no image command — that capability is not reachable from here. Do not promise it.
Anything needing AI Studio, which is a website, not a callable surface.
gemini.notes: Gemini CLI's Google login was retired 2026-06-18 for consumer tiers; Antigravity CLI is the only subscription login path. GEMINI_API_KEY is the metered alternative. Note ~17k input tokens of fixed overhead per headless call, which burns quota faster than the prompt size suggests.

grok.label: Grok (xAI, via Grok Build CLI)
grok.loginCmd: grok login  (SuperGrok or X Premium+ account)
grok.specialism: THE SCOUT — the live world, right now
routeFor: Anything whose answer is happening NOW: is this service degraded for other people, is this breaking change biting anyone, what are developers actually saying about this library.
Native X search and web search are built-in tools, not add-ons. Live access to X posts and developer chatter is the one thing no other provider has.
Contrarian angles — a deliberately different read on a design or conclusion.
Very large single-pass reads (2M context) where Gemini is busy or unavailable.
neverRouteFor: ESTABLISHING FACTS. Grok measured ~64% hallucination on AA-Omniscience where Claude measured 0%. It is fast and confidently wrong often enough that its output must never be treated as settled.
Anything that feeds a decision without a Claude verification pass in between.
grok.outputContract: LEAD, NOT FACT. Everything Grok returns is a lead to verify, never a finding to act on. Report it as 'Grok reports X — unverified' and ground it before it reaches a decision. This is not optional politeness; it is the documented failure mode of this provider.
grok.notes: A consumer SuperGrok / X Premium+ subscription does NOT include xAI API credits — they are separate billing tracks. Sign in; do not buy API credits to use this. Grok Build natively reads AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md and ~/.claude/skills — Alfred's charter already loads in it (verified via 'grok inspect').

codex.label: Codex (OpenAI)
codex.loginCmd: codex login  (add --device-code if no browser is available)
codex.notes: Included at no extra cost with ChatGPT Plus/Pro/Business/Edu/Enterprise. Headless is 'codex exec', which never prompts — so --sandbox is the safety control there.

omniroute.label: OmniRoute (self-hosted gateway to ~340 providers)
omniroute.loginCmd: npm install -g omniroute, then 'omniroute' to start the gateway; connect providers in the dashboard at http://localhost:20128
omniroute.specialism: THE RESERVE — capacity when the bench is empty, and a deliberately different take
omniroute.gate: LAST RESORT OR DELIBERATE CHOICE — never a default, never a convenience.
routeFor: EXHAUSTION: Claude AND Gemini AND Grok are all out of usage. Not one of them — all three. This is the primary reason this provider exists.
DELIBERATE ALTERNATIVE: the operator explicitly wants a community/open-source model's take on something, as a different perspective rather than as a cheaper one.
neverRouteFor: Anything, ever, while Claude has capacity. This is not an overflow valve for convenience or cost — Gemini's overflowModels are the sanctioned overflow path and they serve Claude models on Google's subscription.

ANY work touching secrets, credentials, client data, or a WORK-mode context. The gateway is local but the providers behind it are third parties, and its free tiers are precisely the ones with the least favourable data terms.
Establishing facts. Same rule as Grok: output is a lead to verify, not a finding.
omniroute.outputContract: DRAFT ONLY, PROVENANCE NAMED. Always report which underlying model actually answered — the gateway routes dynamically, so 'OmniRoute said X' is not a source. Say 'OmniRoute via <model> reports X — unverified'.
notes: Self-hosted: `npm install -g omniroute` then `omniroute` runs a local gateway on port 20128 exposing an OpenAI-compatible API. Nothing is proxied through a vendor's server — but the PROVIDERS it forwards to are third parties, so the data-handling rule above still binds fully.

Added 2026-08-16 at the operator's explicit instruction, with exactly the two routing conditions above. The conditions are the point of the entry: without them this is a general-purpose cheap-tokens valve, which is the thing Alfred's Claude-first rule exists to prevent.
'auto' model selection is available but should NOT be used — it makes the answering model unknowable, which breaks the output contract above. Name a model explicitly.
MIT licensed. Free tiers exist (Kiro AI, OpenCode Free); treat any free tier as having unfavourable data terms until its terms are read.

ollama.label: Ollama (local models)
ollama.loginCmd: none needed — run 'ollama serve', then 'ollama pull <model>'
ollama.notes: Free and private — nothing leaves the machine, so no approval gate. Batch workers: a cold model load costs 1-2 min, so batch calls rather than making one-off latency-sensitive ones.
